reviews.explanation: The task is SWE-bench django__django-10097: make core.validators.URLValidator reject ':', '@', '/' in the username/password part. The verifier (tests/test.sh) applies the official test patch (6 new invalid URLs in tests/validators/invalid_urls.txt, 1 changed valid URL), runs the full Django suite, and a swebench-4.0.3 parser requires ALL 438 FAIL_TO_PASS and ALL 1432 PASS_TO_PASS tests from tests/config.json to pass. The stated requirement is never checked: the only tests that exercise it are the dynamically generated test_URLValidator_raises_error_352..357 (validators.tests.TestSimpleValidators) built from the new invalid_urls.txt lines, and neither F2P nor P2P contains any validators.tests entry (searched for 'URLValidator', 'SimpleValidators', 'validators.tests' - zero hits). I reproduced both verifier scenarios in this environment (test patch applied, egg reinstalled, full suite run exactly like test.sh): on the UNFIXED base code, 431 of the 438 F2P tests (auth_tests, model_forms, expressions, cache, syndication_tests, etc. - all unrelated to URL validation) and 1427 of the 1432 P2P tests already pass; exactly the 6 real URLValidator tests fail (visible in the log but ungated). Consequently, the verifier can be satisfied without solving the task at all: it resets only the two URL .txt files and runs the tests from /testbed/tests, so a patch that leaves URLValidator still accepting 'http://foo/bar@example.com' but edits tests/auth_tests/test_templates.py and tests/generic_inline_admin/tests.py (the only 12 gated tests that fail on base) would be reported resolved - a fabricated, plausibly-shaped change passes. Secondary defect (INSTR-VERIFIER-MISMATCH): those same 12 gated tests (7 in F2P: auth_tests.test_templates.AuthTemplateTests; 5 in P2P: generic_inline_admin.tests) ERROR deterministically in BOTH the base and the reference-solution runs with 'sqlite3.OperationalError: no such table: main.django_site__old' and cascading TemplateDoesNotExist - a full-suite test-ordering state leak in this Django 2.2/Python 3.5 environment, unrelated to the URL change (base: failures=53, errors=383; gold: failures=47, errors=383; identical 12 gated ERRORs; the same modules pass in isolation: 'Ran 55 tests ... OK'). Thus even the reference solution fails the verifier, because it gates on tests the instruction does not imply; the primary defect is that the verifier's pass criteria are decoupled from the requirement it is supposed to verify.

reviews.explanation: The verifier's resolution criteria contradict the instruction, so a faithful (even the reference oracle) solution still fails. Evidence: (1) The instruction requires making Django's URLValidator reject unencoded ':' '@' '/' in the userinfo (e.g. http://foo/bar@example.com, PR #10097). In /testbed (django at base commit b9cf764, verified clean) the bug is present: all 6 URLs the test patch adds to tests/validators/invalid_urls.txt are wrongly accepted. The test patch is only exercised by tests dynamically generated from those txt files; I applied the verifier's actual runtime patch (executing test.sh's embedded echo statement verbatim; it applies cleanly, `git apply --check` exit 0) and confirmed the bug-sensitive tests are exactly test_URLValidator_raises_error_352..357 (validators.tests.TestSimpleValidators): they FAIL on base code (6 failures) and pass after applying the oracle regex fix from solution/solve.sh (371 tests OK). (2) tests/config.json FAIL_TO_PASS (the parser's sole grading source) contains NONE of these 6 tests and not a single validators.tests entry; it holds 438 unrelated tests (auth_tests, model_forms, expressions, cache, file_storage, syndication, ...), and PASS_TO_PASS holds 1432 unrelated tests. Worse, both fields are double-serialized JSON strings (32,591 and 107,484 characters), not the JSON arrays the swebench==4.0.3 harness (make_test_spec/get_logs_eval/get_eval_tests_report in tests/test.sh) expects. Iterating them yields single characters (or quote/bracket-laden comma fragments) that can never match Django test-log lines, so zero of the referenced tests is ever counted as passed; under SWE-bench's resolution rule (all F2P and all P2P must pass), the check is unsatisfiable: even with the oracle patch applied, grading yields 0/32591 F2P passed -> NOT_RESOLVED -> parser exits 1 -> reward 0 (simulated both base and oracle runs: resolved=False in both). Thus the verifier checks something the instruction does not imply (438 unrelated tests) and requires the instructed behavior (the 6 validators.tests tests) never to be part of the criteria, and a correct solution still fails. Secondary defect (VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK in spirit): if the string fields were decoded into proper lists, the criteria would still pass an empty no-op patch, because none of the 438 F2P / 1432 P2P tests distinguishes fixed from unfixed code - the verifier would not check any requirement stated in the instruction. Minor non-issues verified: the quote-mangling of the embedded test patch is self-consistent with the repo blob (line 51 is &'() in the base commit and in the runtime patch), so the test patch applies; /testbed, setup.sh, and the environment otherwise provide everything needed.

reviews.explanation: The verifier does not check the requirement stated in the instructions at all, so the task passes without being solved. The instruction (SWE-bench ticket django__django-10097) asks to make core.validators.URLValidator reject unencoded ':', '@', '/' in the URL username/password. The tests that actually verify this requirement are the tests/validators tests: with the verifier's own test patch applied, I confirmed that on the unmodified base commit 6 tests fail (validators.tests.TestSimpleValidators.test_URLValidator_raises_error_352..357, asserting e.g. "ValidationError not raised when validating 'http://foo/bar@example.com'"), and that they all pass after applying the one-line regex fix from solution/solve.sh. However, the verifier (tests/test.sh + tests/config.json, which drives the swebench get_resolution_status check) only scores the 438 FAIL_TO_PASS and 1432 PASS_TO_PASS tests - and config.json contains ZERO entries from validators.tests (no test_valid_urls/test_invalid_urls/ValidatorTests occurrences). The lists were clearly built from dataset-generation runs that died before reaching the alphabetically-later 'validators' module: the PASS_TO_PASS module list ends at urlpatterns_reverse.tests ('u') and FAIL_TO_PASS ends at update.tests, with no modules after that. I then ran every module/class containing any of the 438 F2P tests and all 115 modules/classes containing the 1432 P2P tests against the unmodified base code (test patch applied, with the verifier's exact LANG/LC_ALL/PYTHONIOENCODING environment): all pass (the only errors observed were isolation artifacts - missing django_site__old table - in tests that are not in the scored lists). None of the target test modules even contain a URL with userinfo, so applying or omitting the fix changes no scored test's outcome. Consequence: an agent that makes no change at all (empty patch) will have all 438 F2P and 1432 P2P tests pass and the verifier prints PASSED - a fabricated/no-op 'solution' passes, i.e. the verifier passes without the task actually being solved. Secondary observations: the F2P list is dominated by ~425 tests in unrelated modules (auth_tests, model_forms, expressions, syndication, m2m, etc.) that are artifacts of the truncated generation runs rather than tests of the instructed behavior; and the verifier's 3000s budget for a full --parallel 1 suite (which in this 1-CPU environment was still creating its ~2500 test tables after ~3 minutes) is a timing risk, but the primary defect is that the scored test set is entirely disconnected from the required fix.

reviews.explanation: The instruction (SWE-bench django__django-10914: 'Set default FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSION to 0o644') is faithfully solvable, but the verifier can never accept a correct solution because its reference data is corrupted. I verified the task core by running the Django suite in this environment: at the base commit (e7fd69d) with the verifier's test patch applied (tests/test_utils/tests.py assertion changed from assertIsNone to assertEqual(default_storage.file_permissions_mode, 0o644)), exactly one test fails (test_override_file_upload_permissions, 'None != 420'); after applying the instructed fix (FILE_UPLOAD_PERMISSIONS = 0o644 in django/conf/global_settings.py, exactly what solution/solve.sh does), all 100 tests in test_utils.tests pass. However, in tests/config.json the FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS fields are not the JSON arrays the swebench 4.0.3 harness API used by tests/test.sh expects; they are double-encoded JSON strings (raw file shows: "FAIL_TO_PASS": "[\"test_override_file_upload_permissions (test_utils.tests.OverrideSettingsTests)\"]", and a 6650-char string for PASS_TO_PASS containing 98 test names). parser.py feeds test_spec.FAIL_TO_PASS / test_spec.PASS_TO_PASS (sourced from these fields) into get_eval_tests_report + get_resolution_status, which require ResolvedStatus.FULL. With the string values as shipped, grading either iterates the strings character-by-character (82 + 6650 pseudo 'tests' named '[', '"', 't', 'e', ... that can never match any parsed test result, so every status is empty) or falls back to empty lists, in which case get_resolution_status short-circuits on both-empty lists. Both paths yield UNRESOLVED, so resolved stays False, the script prints FAILED, exits 1, and reward.txt is 0 even with the oracle patch applied. I confirmed this with a faithful simulation of the swebench 4.0.3 grading flow: a control run using properly parsed lists correctly scores the fixed state 'full' and the base state 'unresolved' (proving the simulation matches the harness's intended semantics), while the config.json values as shipped score 'unresolved' in BOTH the base and fixed states. Thus the verifier effectively checks 6732 single-character 'test' requirements that the instruction implies nothing about, and a solution that faithfully follows the instruction (the one-line settings change, verified to make the real FAIL_TO_PASS test pass) still fails the verifier. Secondary observations (not the primary defect): the instruction title itself states the expected change, making the underlying fix small (a single line in global_settings.py), and tests/test.sh has minor cosmetic sloppiness (duplicate shebang, duplicated 'exec 1>&3 2>&4' lines) that does not affect correctness.

reviews.explanation: The task is a SWE-bench-style Django bug fix (django__django-11119): make Engine.render_to_string() honor the engine's autoescape attribute. The core behavioral verification is sound: I confirmed the hidden FAIL_TO_PASS test test_autoescape_off fails at the base commit d4df5e1b (AssertionError: 'obj:<script>\n' != 'obj:<script>\n') and passes with the reference fix (Context(context, autoescape=self.autoescape)), with all 7 PASS_TO_PASS tests green. There is no instruction/verifier mismatch, no ambiguity, no triviality, and no answer leak (a filesystem-wide grep found no 'autoescape=self.autoescape' outside the hidden task folder, the hidden test is absent from the base-commit test files, /tests is empty, and the 'test_autoescape_off' hits in filter_tests are unrelated pre-existing filter tests). The primary defect is environmental: the verifier's final grading stage (tests/test.sh) executes 'uv run parser.py' on a PEP 723 script requiring swebench==4.0.3, datasets==2.16.1, fastcore<1.11 (and Python >=3.11) fetched over the network. The environment provides no network: DNS fails ('curl: (6) Could not resolve host: pypi.org'), raw TCP egress to 8.8.8.8:53 and 1.1.1.1:443 times out, no proxy is configured, there is no local mirror or wheelhouse, the packages are not installed in any conda environment, and uv's cache is empty. I reproduced the failure directly: 'uv run parser.py' dies with 'Failed to fetch https://pypi.org/simple/datasets/ ... dns error' (exit 2), and 'uv run --offline parser.py' reports 'swebench was not found in the cache ... network was disabled' (exit 1). Consequently test.sh always writes reward 0 and exits nonzero no matter how correct the patch in /testbed is - even the oracle fix, which I verified makes every test pass, can never be graded as resolved. The agent cannot remedy this by installing or configuring available components: nothing needed is available locally, and the verifier runs in a separate environment (task.toml environment_mode = 'separate') that /testbed changes cannot reach. The verifier therefore depends on a network/PyPI service the environment does not actually provide, so the task cannot be completed and verified as written.

reviews.explanation: This is SWE-bench instance django__django-11206: fix django.utils.numberformat.format so that a Decimal whose absolute value is smaller than what decimal_pos can represent renders as '0.00...0' instead of exponential notation. I verified the full loop in the actual environment: (1) /testbed is at the exact base commit 571ab44 with the buggy code, the conda 'testbed' env and ./tests/runtests.py work, and the test patch applies cleanly (git apply --check); (2) pre-fix, with the test patch applied, test_decimal_numbers fails with exactly the reported bug (AssertionError: '1.234e-300' != '0.000'); (3) with the reference solution patch, all 6 tests in utils_tests.test_numberformat pass, including both FAIL_TO_PASS tests, and the P2P tests (large-number exponential behavior like '1.000e+300') are preserved. Verifier discrimination was verified by emulating the swebench 4.0.3 grading used by tests/test.sh (parse_log_django: line startswith 'test' + contains ' ... ok' -> first token added to pass set; F2P/P2P matched by first token; FULL resolution requires all to pass): the pre-fix log yields resolved=False (reward 0) and the post-fix log yields resolved=True (reward 1). Notably, a Python 3.6 quirk (addSubTest records failures without printing the parent's progress token) merges the failing test_decimal_numbers progress line with the following '... ok' line, so the failing test is miscounted as passing in the log parse; however the second FAIL_TO_PASS test test_decimal_subclass then never appears at the start of any line and is counted as failing, so the unsolved state is still rejected, and an adversarial edge case (both F2P tests broken) is also rejected — hence not VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK. The patched test's expectation '0.000' is exactly the behavior the instruction requests, so no INSTR-VERIFIER-MISMATCH; the verifier resets the test file before applying the test patch, neutralizing test tampering. The environment provides everything referenced (repo at base commit, conda env, locale-gen, uv, allow_internet=true for the 'uv run parser.py' step, which the Dockerfile build itself requires), so no INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH. The instruction contains only the bug report, not the fix; the solution exists only in solution/solve.sh and the verifier-side config.json, which are not agent-visible, so no ANSWER-LEAK. The task is a genuine debugging exercise (understanding Decimal formatting and the hardcoded >200-digit scientific-notation branch), so not TASK-TRIVIAL, and the requested behavior is precisely specified, so not INSTR-AMBIGUOUS.

reviews.explanation: The task core is sound (I verified it end-to-end in a scratch clone): /testbed sits at the base commit 53d8646 with the conda 'testbed' env (py3.6, Django 3.1 dev install), the test patch embedded in tests/test.sh applies cleanly (I evaluated the exact echo statement and ran git apply --check), both FAIL_TO_PASS tests (test_use_required_attribute, test_filefield_with_fileinput_required) FAIL in the unsolved state, and the oracle patch from solution/solve.sh makes the whole targeted suite pass (all 117 PASS_TO_PASS and 2 FAIL_TO_PASS entries, including the two doctest-style names, appear in the log as 'name (module.Class) ... ok'). The defect is in the verifier's grading plumbing: tests/config.json stores FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS as double-encoded JSON strings (e.g. "FAIL_TO_PASS": "[\"test_use_required_attribute (forms_tests.widget_tests.test_fileinput.FileInputTest)\", ...]"), not JSON arrays, while the parser in tests/test.sh feeds this file straight into the swebench==4.0.3 harness (datum = json.load(...); test_spec = make_test_spec(datum); get_eval_tests_report(...); get_resolution_status(...)). reviews.explanation: This is a well-formed SWE-bench-style task (django/django-12304: enum/Choices types unusable in Django templates). I verified the environment matches the instruction: /testbed is at base commit 4c1b401e with a working conda 'testbed' env, and the bug reproduces (the FAIL_TO_PASS test test_templates fails pre-fix with output '|' != 'Diamond|1'). The verifier is strong and behavior-based: it applies the official test patch, runs the real Django suite (model_enums.tests), and grades via the SWE-bench parser on FAIL_TO_PASS 'test_templates (model_enums.tests.ChoicesTests)' plus 17 PASS_TO_PASS tests; I confirmed the test fails before the fix and all 18 tests pass after applying the reference one-line fix, so fabricated output could not pass (not VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK). The verifier checks exactly what the issue implies (enums usable in templates, e.g. {{ Suit.DIAMOND.label }}), so there is no INSTR-VERIFIER-MISMATCH, and no missing paths/services (no INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH). The borderline concern is that the issue's last line hints at the mechanism ('declare do_not_call_in_templates = True on the various Choices classes'), which could suggest ANSWER-LEAK. However, the expected answer is NOT fully revealed: I demonstrated that the literal reading (adding the attribute to the Choices class body) breaks the codebase entirely — 'import django.db.models' crashes with TypeError: Cannot extend enumerations because enum treats class-body names as members, and enums with members cannot be extended. The actual fix requires understanding that the attribute must be assigned on cls inside ChoicesMeta.__new__ (post class creation), so it applies to every generated enum class without becoming a member. An agent following the instruction must still reproduce the bug, implement the hint, hit this enum pitfall, and derive the metaclass placement — genuine (modest) debugging work, so neither ANSWER-LEAK nor TASK-TRIVIAL applies. No solution or verifier files are shipped to the agent (they live only in the hidden review folder), and grepping the repo shows do_not_call_in_templates only in pre-existing, unrelated consumers (template engine, descriptor classes). No defect from the rubric is present.

reviews.explanation: The task (SWE-bench django__django-13089: fix 'NoneType' object is not subscriptable in django/core/cache/backends/db.py _cull()) is itself well-posed and solvable, but the verifier cannot produce a passing verdict in the provided environment because its final grading step depends on a network service the environment does not provide. tests/test.sh ends with `uv run parser.py`, where parser.py is an inline script declaring dependencies swebench==4.0.3, datasets==2.16.1, fastcore<1.11 that uv must download from PyPI on first run. The evaluation environment is completely offline: /etc/resolv.conf is empty, DNS lookups fail (getent/curl/python socket all report 'Temporary failure in name resolution'), raw outbound TCP to 8.8.8.8:53, 1.1.1.1:443 and a pinned PyPI IP:443 all time out, no proxy env vars or local PyPI mirror/proxy exist on localhost, and none of the grading packages is pre-provisioned anywhere (swebench is in no conda env; `find / -name '*swebench*'` finds nothing; the uv cache is an empty 120K; the 29M pip cache contains only unrelated wheels). I reproduced the exact verifier step: `uv run parser.py` (extracted verbatim from test.sh, with /tests/config.json and a LOG_FILE) exits with code 2 ('Failed to fetch https://pypi.org/simple/... dns error') before any test grading occurs; test.sh then exits with that code and writes reward 0, so even the perfect oracle solution is marked FAILED. Because task.toml sets [verifier] environment_mode="separate" with artifacts=["/testbed"], the agent cannot modify the verifier container or pre-seed caches — only the /testbed patch is carried over, and no change to Django source can provide internet access. This is precisely a dependency/service (PyPI/internet, declared via allow_internet=true but not actually delivered) that the environment fails to provide, making the task uncompletable as written. Supporting evidence that the rest of the task is sound (so this is the primary defect): on the base commit the new regression test test_cull_delete_when_store_empty fails with the exact reported TypeError in db.py:272, and applying the reference fix makes both FAIL_TO_PASS tests pass plus all cache test classes pass (DBCacheTests 57 OK, DBCacheWithTimeZoneTests OK, LocMemCacheTests+DummyCacheTests 81 OK, FileBasedCacheTests+FileBasedCachePathLibTests 116 OK, CacheI18n/Utils/Middleware/FragmentKey 40 OK, remaining classes OK with expected memcached/pylibmc skips), i.e., the verifier's test logic would grade the fix correctly if it could run. A secondary anomaly investigated and ruled out: long test runs in this sandbox die with 'semop(1): encountered an error: Invalid argument' — I traced this to the Apptainer/fakeroot wrapper (LD_PRELOAD libfakeroot + per-session faked daemon + System V semaphore destroyed at session teardown) and it only affects processes that outlive their launching session; all in-session, production-equivalent test runs completed cleanly, so it is a review-sandbox artifact, not a task defect.

reviews.explanation: The task itself is sound, but the verifier is broken such that a faithful solution still fails. The instruction (Django issue 13109) asks to make ForeignKey.validate() use the base manager instead of the default manager (django/db/models/fields/related.py line 917). I verified the environment provides everything needed (/testbed at base commit fbe82f82, conda 'testbed' env, uv) and that the task is genuinely solvable: after applying the shipped test patch, both FAIL_TO_PASS tests fail on unfixed code ('author instance with id 1 does not exist.'), and after applying the reference one-line fix (_default_manager -> _base_manager), the entire verifier test scope (model_forms.models model_forms.tests validation.models validation.tests) passes: 'Ran 173 tests ... OK' (170 PASS_TO_PASS + 3 new tests). The fatal defect is in the verifier's grading data: tests/config.json (read by the parser as /tests/config.json) stores FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS as double-encoded JSON strings instead of JSON arrays (raw file content: '"FAIL_TO_PASS": "[\"test_FK_validates_using_base_manager (validation.tests.BaseModelValidationTests)\", ...]"'; json.load returns type str for both fields). The parser delegates to swebench==4.0.3, whose make_test_spec() computes FAIL_TO_PASS=sorted(set(instance[KEY_FAIL_TO_PASS])) and PASS_TO_PASS=sorted(set(instance[KEY_PASS_TO_PASS])); applied to strings this yields a sorted list of unique single characters (36 'tests' for FAIL_TO_PASS such as 'F', '(', ','; 65 for PASS_TO_PASS). get_eval_tests_report() then requires each of these character 'test names' to appear in the parsed test log as passed, which is impossible, so report[FAIL_TO_PASS]['passed'] is always 0 < total, get_resolution_status() always returns UNRESOLVED, and test.sh always prints FAILED and writes reward 0. I reproduced this by simulating the exact swebench 4.0.3 grading logic against the real captured log with the gold patch applied (all 173 tests passing): FAIL_TO_PASS {total: 36, passed: 0}, PASS_TO_PASS {total: 65, passed: 0} -> UNRESOLVED -> FAILED. Thus the verifier checks something the instruction does not imply (test-log entries whose names are single characters of a config string) and contradicts it: even the oracle/reference patch, which I confirmed passes every intended test, is scored FAILED. A secondary, adjacent defect is INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH in the sense that the environment ships a corrupted config.json where the standard swebench grading glue assumes a valid instance row with proper lists, and the agent cannot repair it (verifier environment is separate and private); the instruction also nearly states the fix ('Suggested solution: use the _base_manager'), which is a strong hint but not a full answer leak. The primary defect remains the verifier/grading mismatch that makes the task unsolvable regardless of the agent's work.

I verified the pieces individually work: /testbed is at the correct base commit with a working conda env; the test patch embedded in tests/test.sh (with its '"'"' shell-escaping) expands to a diff that `git apply --check`/`git apply` accept; with base code the new test test_token_with_different_email fails (3 subtests); applying the oracle patch from solution/solve.sh yields 58/58 tests OK. However, the verifier's own log capture deterministically corrupts one PASS_TO_PASS test, so no faithful solution can ever be graded resolved. tests/test.sh records the run with `exec > >(tee "$LOG_FILE") 2>&1`. In Django 3.2 the verbose test-status lines go to stderr (DiscoverRunner passes no stream to TextTestRunner; confirmed empirically: '... ok' lines only in stderr) while 'System check identified no issues (0 silenced).' is written to stdout (django/core/management/base.py:477 self.stdout.write(msg); confirmed empirically: message only in stdout). Because both streams are block-buffered in this CPython 3.6, in the merged log the stdout message lands between the '... ' and the 'ok' of a stderr line, producing exactly: 'test_email_user (auth_tests.test_models.AbstractUserTestCase) ... System check identified no issues (0 silenced).\nok'. I reproduced this in 6/6 runs (base and fixed states, plain redirect, and the exact tee redirection used by test.sh), always at log line 78. 'test_email_user (auth_tests.test_models.AbstractUserTestCase)' is one of the 56 PASS_TO_PASS entries in tests/config.json, and the verifier's swebench-4.0.3 grading (get_logs_eval/get_eval_tests_report/get_resolution_status with EvalType.PASS_AND_FAIL for django) requires every PASS_TO_PASS test to be extractable from the log as passed. Under any line-based parser the corrupted line yields status 'System...' or the test is absent (I simulated 4 parser styles: anchored regex, unanchored regex, rsplit on ' ... ', and ok|FAIL|ERROR alternation; none can see the test as 'ok'; the literal string '... ... ok' is not present in the log). Consequently the report can never reach 'fully resolved', the parser prints FAILED and writes reward 0 even for the oracle fix that empirically passes 58/58. A solution that faithfully follows the instruction still fails the verifier. Secondary, non-primary issues: (1) FAIL_TO_PASS wrongly lists test_token_with_different_secret, which already passes pre-fix (harmless by itself since the grader only requires it to pass in the final run); (2) the first FAIL_TO_PASS entry is docstring-only ('Updating the user email address invalidates the token.'), which depends on the harness performing docstring-based test matching - fragile but not independently verifiable in this offline review environment; (3) the ticket text hints at the function to change, but that is a hint, not the full solution (custom/absent email fields must still be handled correctly), so it is not an ANSWER-LEAK.

reviews.explanation: The verifier (tests/test.sh) applies the SWE-bench test patch for django__django-13551, runs ./tests/runtests.py (4 auth test modules, 58 tests), and then grades the log with swebench 4.0.3's get_logs_eval/get_eval_tests_report/get_resolution_status. I reproduced the full flow in the task's own workspace (copy of /testbed at the base commit 7f9e4524): (1) The key behavioral requirement is only enforced by the new test test_token_with_different_email, whose log identity is its docstring 'Updating the user email address invalidates the token.' (that exact string is the FAIL_TO_PASS entry). When the test FAILS (i.e., the bug is present), unittest writes 'Updating the user email address invalidates the token. ... ' and the next test's startTest output is glued onto the same line: "Updating the user email address invalidates the token. ... test_token_with_different_secret (auth_tests.test_tokens.TokenGeneratorTest) ... ok" - there is no line of the form '<docstring> ... FAIL' anywhere (the FAIL summary block prints the docstring on a bare line with no status token). Any line parser consistent with the official FAIL_TO_PASS list (which contains this docstring id and the pre-existing test_token_with_different_secret, the latter only 'failing' at base because its ' ... ok' line is likewise absorbed into that glued line) therefore attributes NO status to either FAIL_TO_PASS id in the no-fix run; they are simply absent from the parsed status map. (2) The classic SWE-bench report builder that test.sh's parser calls skips tests not present in the status map (list comprehension guarded by 'if test in eval_status_map'), so with both F2P ids absent and no explicit failure among the 55 cleanly parseable PASS_TO_PASS lines, get_resolution_status returns FULL. I simulated exactly this grading over the real no-fix log: resolved=True, i.e. the verifier would print PASSED, write reward=1, and exit 0 for a no-op agent that never touches the code - the task's stated requirement (email change must invalidate password reset tokens) is effectively never checked. (3) The log tracking is additionally corrupted by an environment artifact: Django prints 'System check identified no issues (0 silenced).' to block-buffered stdout while unittest writes test progress to stderr; in this image the message consistently (7/7 runs, including an exact replication of test.sh's 'exec > >(tee $LOG_FILE) 2>&1' capture) lands mid-line, e.g. 'test_email_user (auth_tests.test_models.AbstractUserTestCase) ... System check identified no issues (0 silenced).' followed by 'ok' on its own line, so even that PASS_TO_PASS test's status is unparseable in the fixed state (and test_check_password_upgrade's in the unfixed state). With a missing-tests-count-as-failed grading policy this same artifact would instead make even the oracle solution (verified: all 58 tests pass with the reference patch) fail verification - under either policy the verifier's log parsing does not match the environment's actual log output, but with the SWE-bench harness's actual skip-missing semantics the dominant observable defect is that the verifier passes without the task being solved.

OK (skipped=2)). However, the verifier's grading gate can never succeed regardless of the solution. tests/test.sh records ONLY the stdout/stderr of './tests/runtests.py --settings=test_sqlite custom_pk.fields custom_pk.models custom_pk.tests' into LOG_FILE (the test-patch echo/apply happens before log capture begins), and its parser then calls swebench 4.0.3's get_logs_eval(test_spec, log_path). In swebench 4.0.3, get_logs_eval delegates to _get_patch_diff_from_log, which requires the log to contain '>>>> Patch Diff Start ... >>>> Patch Diff End' (model patch) and '>>>> Test Patch Diff Start ... >>>> Test Patch Diff End' (test patch text) sections in addition to the __START_TEST_OUTPUT__/__END_TEST_OUTPUT__ block - the log format that swebench's own run_evaluation harness appends to instance logs, which is also what the harness uses for its 'test_evals_found' ('whether the log contained the correct test patch, test start, and test end') and 'patch_successfully_applied' report fields. I reproduced the exact verifier flow and captured the resulting log: it contains 0 occurrences of 'Patch Diff' and 0 occurrences of the test-patch text (only the raw unittest output, which the parser itself wraps with the START/END markers). Consequently _get_patch_diff_from_log prints 'Could not find model patch in log file' and returns (None, None, None), so get_logs_eval either raises the 'Repo mismatch'/'Test patch mismatch' assertion or yields found=False; the parser's 'if found:' block never executes, 'resolved' stays False, the parser prints FAILED and exits 1, and reward.txt is written as 0. Nothing the agent does in /testbed can add those log sections (LOG_FILE is created and populated solely by test.sh in the verifier container), so even the oracle fix - which I verified makes every real test pass - scores 0: a solution that faithfully follows the instructions still fails because the verifier demands a log format that neither the instructions nor the verifier's own script ever produces. The defect is in the verifier's own grading chain, which makes the task unpassable even for a faithful solution: (1) tests/config.json stores FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS as JSON *strings* (serialized lists — confirmed: json.load returns str for both), while the parser embedded in tests/test.sh immediately calls make_test_spec(datum) from the pinned swebench==4.0.3 without any conversion; swebench 4.0.3's make_test_spec builds a pydantic TestSpec model whose FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS fields are typed list[str], and pydantic v2 rejects str input for a list field ('Input should be a valid list'), so the parser crashes with a ValidationError before it can score the run, 'uv run parser.py' exits non-zero, and the verifier unconditionally reports FAILED/reward 0. The agent cannot work around this because environment_mode='separate': the agent only ever modifies /testbed, while /tests/config.json and test.sh are applied by the harness in the verifier container. (2) A second latent break in the same chain: 2 of the 76 PASS_TO_PASS entries are docstring lines rather than 'name (module.Class)' test ids ('Extract year uses a BETWEEN filter to compare the year to allow indexes' and 'If the truncated datetime transitions to a different offset (daylight'); I confirmed these only appear in the runtests log as standalone '<docstring> ... ok' lines emitted by Django's verbosity-2 runner). In every failure mode a solution that faithfully follows the instruction still fails, which is the defining condition of INSTR-VERIFIER-MISMATCH. reviews.explanation: The instruction (the Django ticket) states a specific requirement: the MySQL backend uses deprecated 'db' and 'passwd' kwargs 'seen at django/db/backends/mysql/base.py#L202-L205' and they should be replaced with 'database' and 'password' for mysqlclient. The verifier, however, checks none of that: every FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS test in tests/config.json lives in tests/dbshell/test_mysql.py and only exercises DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env in django/db/backends/mysql/client.py (the dbshell CLI argument builder), which the instruction never mentions. I verified this empirically in the provided environment (/testbed at base commit d06c5b35, conda 'testbed' env, running ./tests/runtests.py --settings=test_sqlite dbshell.test_mysql with the hidden test patch applied): (1) base state fails 2 of the 3 FAIL_TO_PASS tests and the oracle solution (base.py + client.py) makes all 9 tests pass, so the harness machinery itself works; (2) a solution that faithfully implements exactly what the instruction describes - changing kwargs['db']->kwargs['database'] and kwargs['passwd']->kwargs['password'] in base.py get_connection_params - still FAILS the two FAIL_TO_PASS tests (test_options_non_deprecated_keys_preferred and test_options_override_settings_proper_values), because those tests require the unstated client.py behavior of honoring OPTIONS['database'] (falling back to 'db'/NAME) and preferring the non-deprecated key names; (3) conversely, applying only the client.py change while leaving the deprecated kwargs at base.py lines 203/205 intact passes the entire verifier. So the verifier checks behavior the instruction does not imply (a faithful solution still fails) - the primary defect. The mirror-image weakness is secondary (VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK): the actually stated requirement is never checked, and mysqlclient is not even installed (no MySQLDB module, no MySQL server, runtests uses test_sqlite), so the instructed fix is untestable in this environment and a patch that leaves it broken still earns reward 1. Not INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH: /testbed, the pinned base commit, and the test runner all exist and work; the verifier's runtime internet needs (pip install -e . and 'uv run' fetching swebench 4.0.3) are covered by the task's allow_internet=true, though the script's 'set -e' plus 'pip install -e .' is a fragility if the network is absent. Not ANSWER-LEAK (instruction is only the ticket text; solution/test patches are not shipped in the workspace), not TASK-TRIVIAL, and the inclusion of test_parameters in FAIL_TO_PASS despite it already passing at base is a harmless dataset artifact that only tightens the bar.

I reproduced this empirically in the task environment: with the test patch applied and only the client.py hunk of the reference patch present (base.py left pristine, still emitting kwargs['db']/kwargs['passwd'] at the exact lines the instruction cites), all 3 FAIL_TO_PASS and all 6 PASS_TO_PASS tests pass (Ran 9 tests ... OK), so the swebench-based grader awards reward=1 even though the reported bug - Django passing deprecated kwargs to mysqlclient's connect() - is completely unfixed. The verifier therefore passes without the task actually being solved and does not check the requirement stated in the instruction at its explicitly cited location. Secondary observations: (1) a mild instruction/verifier mismatch flavor exists in the other direction - the tests require client.py to honor new OPTIONS keys ('database'/'password' preferred over 'db'/'passwd'), which the instruction never states; an agent who literally implements only the cited base.py change fails the two F2P tests (verified: FAILED, failures=2), though a complete faithful fix (base.py + client.py, as in the gold patch) does pass; (2) FAIL_TO_PASS includes test_parameters, which the test patch never modifies and which passes even with no fix at all (mislabeled, though harmless since it passes in all states). These are secondary to the primary defect that the instruction's stated base.py requirement is entirely unchecked.

reviews.explanation: The instruction (SWE-bench issue django__django-14376) describes exactly one defect: the MySQL backend passes deprecated 'db' and 'passwd' kwargs to mysqlclient, with the usage explicitly located at django/db/backends/mysql/base.py#L202-L205 (get_connection_params). I verified in the provided environment that a solution faithfully implementing that instruction - changing only kwargs['db']->kwargs['database'] and kwargs['passwd']->kwargs['password'] in base.py - FAILS the verifier: the FAIL_TO_PASS tests test_options_non_deprecated_keys_preferred and test_options_override_settings_proper_values exercise DatabaseClient.settings_to_cmd_args_env in django/db/backends/mysql/client.py (the dbshell argv builder, which never calls mysqlclient) and require OPTIONS to accept a new 'database' key preferred over the deprecated 'db' key - behavior the instruction never states or implies. The instruction does not mention dbshell, DATABASES['OPTIONS'], or client.py at all, so a faithful minimal fix is rejected. Conversely (secondary VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK aspect, same root cause), none of the 9 FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS tests ever executes get_connection_params: I confirmed that a patch touching ONLY client.py passes the entire test suite while base.py still contains the deprecated kwargs['db']/kwargs['passwd'] at lines 203/205 that the instruction calls out, so the verifier marks the task resolved although the stated requirement remains unimplemented. The tests (from the upstream PR) check a broader fix than the instruction implies while simultaneously omitting the instruction's actual requirement. Other categories ruled out: the environment is complete (/testbed at base commit d06c5b3, working conda testbed env, uv installed, /logs/verifier exists; the network-dependent 'pip install -e .' and 'uv run parser.py' steps are covered by allow_internet=true), the reference solution does make all tests pass, git history is truncated at the base commit so the fix is not leakable, and the task is a genuine debugging exercise (not trivial).

reviews.explanation: This is the SWE-bench debugging task django__django-14382 (fix `django-admin startapp name directory/` failing with `CommandError: '' is not a valid app directory` when the target directory has a trailing slash). I verified the environment is sound and the verifier is a real behavior test: the repo is at the base commit, the conda testbed works, and the FAIL_TO_PASS test `test_trailing_slash_in_target_app_directory_name` actually runs `django-admin startapp app apps/app1/`, asserts no error and that `apps.py` is created. I confirmed it FAILS on the unpatched code (AssertionError: CommandError: '' is not a valid app directory) and PASSES with the reference patch (and all 6 StartApp tests pass), so the verifier is not too weak and the environment is not broken. The defect is that the instruction itself (instruction.md, the problem statement) embeds the complete solution: it names the exact file (django/core/management/templates.py), the exact line (line 77), the exact buggy statement (`self.validate_name(os.path.basename(target), 'directory')`), and explicitly gives the fix ('Removing potential trailing slashes would solve the problem: `self.validate_name(os.path.basename(target.rstrip(os.sep)), 'directory')`'). I verified empirically that applying that suggested one-line fix verbatim makes the verifier test pass. Because the answer is spelled out in the instruction, the agent needs no genuine debugging or discovery work — it only has to locate the given file/line and paste in the provided change. This satisfies the ANSWER-LEAK definition ('the instruction itself ... reveals the expected answer ... embeds the solution ... so the task requires no genuine work'). Secondary considerations were checked and ruled out as the primary issue: the task is not intrinsically TASK-TRIVIAL (it is a real debugging task that only becomes trivial because the fix is leaked), and there is no INSTR-VERIFIER-MISMATCH or INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH.

I reproduced the whole flow: without the fix both new tests fail with the exact redirect mismatch the instruction describes ('/test_admin/admin/admin_views/article/' != '/prefix/test_admin/admin/admin_views/article/'); with the reference solution patch all 344 module tests pass (15 Selenium tests skipped as usual), and a faithful re-implementation of swebench's django log parser (line ending in '... ok' = test name, which is also how the 160 docstring-style P2P names were generated, e.g. 'Staff_member_required decorator works with an argument' at tests/admin_views/tests.py:3030) finds all 323 P2P and 2 F2P names as 'ok' => resolved. (3) No answer leak: the agent environment ships only the base-commit repo plus a Dockerfile/setup.sh (checked /testbed, /workspace, /setup_files; no patches, stashes, or solution files); the instruction is the standard SWE-bench problem statement (bug description, not a diff) and the agent must still locate and modify the code. So the verifier is not too weak and matches the instruction, the task is not trivial, and no answer is leaked to the agent. The blocking defect is an unresolvable environment dependency in the verifier: tests/test.sh ends with `uv run parser.py`, a PEP 723 script that requires swebench==4.0.3, datasets==2.16.1 and fastcore<1.11 to be fetched from PyPI at verification time. This environment provides no such service: there is no /etc/resolv.conf, `getent hosts pypi.org` and curl to pypi.org/aliyun/tsinghua mirrors all fail (exit 6, code 000), TCP egress to 8.8.8.8:53 is blocked, the uv cache is empty (only empty skeleton dirs, no wheels/sdists), no .whl files or local package index exist anywhere on disk, and none of the three packages is installed in any conda env (testbed or base). I ran the verifier's exact step: `uv run parser.py` exits 2 with 'Failed to fetch ... Could not connect, are you offline? / dns error'. Because test.sh keeps `set -uo pipefail` active at the `uv run parser.py | tee` pipeline, that nonzero exit is captured (exit_code=2), reward.txt is written as 0, and the script exits 2 - i.e. even a perfectly correct solution is graded FAILED. The agent cannot remedy this (no network, no offline copies of the packages), so the task cannot be completed/verified as written: the verifier depends on a service (PyPI) the environment does not actually provide. Secondary (non-defects worth noting only): the agent-side environment is otherwise fully consistent (buggy code, conda 'testbed' env, runtests.py all present and working offline).

reviews.explanation: The verifier can never return reward 1, so a solution that faithfully follows the instruction still fails. Evidence: (1) In tests/config.json, FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS are stored as JSON-encoded STRINGS, not lists (raw file: "FAIL_TO_PASS": "[\"test_readonly_foreignkey_links_custom_admin_site (admin_views.tests.ReadonlyTest)\"]", and PASS_TO_PASS is a 23704-char string). The parser embedded in tests/test.sh loads this file and passes it to swebench==4.0.3 make_test_spec(), which takes these fields verbatim; get_eval_tests_report() then iterates them as sequences of test names. Iterating a string yields individual characters, so the eval report becomes ~79+ keys like '[', '"', 't', 'e', 's', each mapped to 'NOT RUN' (verified by simulating the exact parser flow with a log produced by a correct solution). get_resolution_status() therefore can never equal FULLY_RESOLVED: resolved stays False, the parser prints 'FAILED' and exits 1, and /logs/verifier/reward.txt gets 0 regardless of the agent's work. (2) The underlying task is otherwise solvable: in the real environment I confirmed test_readonly_foreignkey_links_custom_admin_site (admin_views.tests.ReadonlyTest) FAILs at base commit 475cffd and the gold patch (django/contrib/admin/helpers.py get_admin_url, adding current_app=self.model_admin.admin_site.name) makes it pass, so the verifier's data format - not the task - is the blocker. (3) A second independent verifier defect: 166 of the 325 PASS_TO_PASS entries are test docstrings (e.g. "Admin index views don't break when user's ModelAdmin removes standard urls", "Test for ticket 2445 changes to admin.") rather than 'test_name (module.Class)' ids; they can never match a key in the log-parsed status map, so even with correct list typing they would all report 'NOT RUN' and a strict FULL resolution check under EvalType.PASS_AND_FAIL would still fail. (4) Additional secondary issue: the instruction embeds the exact fix verbatim (the gold patch is literally the code block in the issue text), so the 'debugging' work reduces to pasting the proposed lines into helpers.py, which weakens the task's signal even if the verifier were repaired. The environment itself is fully provided (base image, /testbed at the right commit, conda testbed env, working test runner), so this is a verifier-vs-instruction contradiction, not a missing-resource problem.

reviews.explanation: The verifier depends on network/PyPI services that the task environment does not actually provide, so even the reference (oracle) solution fails verification. Evidence: (1) The runtime environment is offline - DNS resolution fails (getent hosts pypi.org -> exit 2; curl exit 6; python urllib -> 'Temporary failure in name resolution'), there is no proxy, no /etc/pip.conf or local index, the pip cache contains no usable setuptools/wheel, there is no uv cache, and swebench/datasets/fastcore are not installed in any conda env. (2) tests/test.sh's first real step, 'python -m pip install -e .', uses PEP 517 build isolation (pyproject.toml requires setuptools>=40.8.0 + wheel), which must download from PyPI and therefore fails offline. Because 'set -euo pipefail' is set at the top and the later 'set -uo pipefail -x' does NOT clear -e (verified: bash -c 'set -eu; set -uo pipefail -x; false' exits 1), the script aborts immediately on that failure. I ran the full tests/test.sh end-to-end with the oracle solution applied to /testbed: it aborted at 'pip install -e .' with exit code 1 and never reached the test run, yielding reward 0. (3) Even if step 1 were bypassed, the grading step 'uv run parser.py' (PEP 723 inline dependencies swebench==4.0.3, datasets==2.16.1, fastcore<1.11) must also download from PyPI with no cache or preinstall, so it cannot grade a passing test run either. The agent cannot resolve this: no available component provides network or a local mirror, the verifier runs in a separate container where only /testbed is an artifact, and the agent never sees test.sh. Note the core task mechanics are otherwise sound: I reproduced the bug at base commit 5eb6a2b33d (test_select_related_only -> ValueError: 'baseuser_ptr_id' is not in list), confirmed the oracle patch makes the FAIL_TO_PASS test pass and all 30 proxy_models tests (incl. all PASS_TO_PASS) pass, and the test patch applies cleanly. Secondary defects: (a) ANSWER-LEAK - instruction.md (the issue body) embeds a working fix ('At django/db/models/sql/query.py in 745 line there is snippet: opts = cur_model._meta; If I replace it by opts = cur_model._meta.concrete_model._meta all works as expected'); I verified that applying exactly this suggested line passes the regression test, so the expected answer is embedded in the instructions and the task reduces to applying the given one-liner (borderline TASK-TRIVIAL in work content). (b) Minor robustness/ordering bug in the verifier: the parser writes /logs/verifier/report.json before test.sh's 'mkdir -p /logs/verifier' executes, and only works because the harness happens to pre-create that directory.

reviews.explanation: The task is the SWE-bench instance django__django-16145: make `manage.py runserver 0:8000` print 'Starting development server at http://0.0.0.0:8000/'. I verified empirically that the environment is correct (/testbed at base commit 93d4c9ea1d, Django dev-installed in the conda testbed env), that the verifier's hidden test `test_zero_ip_addr (admin_scripts.tests.ManageRunserver)` FAILS without a fix (actual output 'http://0:8000/') and PASSES with the shipped reference patch (full ManageRunserver class 11/11 green). So a faithful solution to the instruction exists and was confirmed to work. However, the verifier cannot accept it: in tests/config.json the grading fields FAIL_TO_PASS ('["test_zero_ip_addr (admin_scripts.tests.ManageRunserver)"]') and PASS_TO_PASS (an 11,823-char JSON-encoded list of 174 test names) are JSON-encoded STRINGS, not the lists of test names that the grading code consumes. tests/test.sh's parser passes test_spec.FAIL_TO_PASS / test_spec.PASS_TO_PASS straight into swebench 4.0.3's get_eval_tests_report and requires get_resolution_status(report) == ResolvedStatus.FULL, whose SWE-bench semantics require every listed F2P/P2P test to be found in the log and pass (ref-list tests missing from the log are reconciled in as failures/'NOT FOUND'). Iterating a string walks its characters: I demonstrated that this produces 57 phantom 'missing' F2P tests and 11,474 phantom 'missing' P2P tests (every character of the two JSON strings is a 'test' absent from any log), so failed_F2P/failed_P2P can never be empty, ResolvedStatus.FULL is unreachable, and the verifier emits reward 0 for every patch - including the reference solution, i.e. a solution that faithfully follows the instruction still fails. Secondary defects reinforcing this: the P2P list also contains a bogus one-character '"' entry (a docstring-parsing artifact that no real test run satisfies as a test named '"'), and the parser step depends on `uv run` downloading swebench==4.0.3 at verify time (allowed by task.toml allow_internet=true; my review sandbox had no network, so that final step was analyzed against the pinned harness semantics plus the demonstrated string-iteration mechanics, while the test-side behavior - patch application, run, fail-without-fix/pass-with-fix - was verified end to end). Not VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK (a bogus patch fails the real F2P test), not INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH (the environment supplies the repo, base commit, and interpreter exactly as the instruction implies; the defect is in the verifier's own grading data/logic), not INSTR-AMBIGUOUS (the issue states the exact expected output), not TASK-TRIVIAL, and no ANSWER-LEAK (the fix commit is absent from /testbed's git object DB and no solution artifacts exist in the agent-visible workspace).

reviews.explanation: The task itself (fix AdminSite.catch_all_view() dropping the query string, Django ticket #31747) is real and solvable: I verified in the shipped environment that /testbed sits at base commit 55bcbd8d17, that both FAIL_TO_PASS tests fail on the buggy code, and that the reference fix (solution/solve.sh) makes them pass, with the verifier's exact command (./tests/runtests.py --verbosity 2 --settings=test_sqlite --parallel 1 admin_views.tests) logging every referenced test name. However, the verifier cannot award reward for any solution, because tests/test.sh's parser feeds /tests/config.json directly to swebench==4.0.3's make_test_spec(), and in that file FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS are stored as JSON-encoded STRINGS, not JSON arrays (verified: json.load yields str of length 340 and 30117). swebench's TestSpec construction does FAIL_TO_PASS=list(instance.get('FAIL_TO_PASS', [])); applied to a string, list() yields the individual characters (['[', '"', 't', 'e', ...]), so the grader looks for 340 'F2P tests' and 30117 'P2P tests' that are single characters. None of those are real test names (simulated against the actual oracle log: at most one character matches), so the SWE-bench resolution check (all FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS found and passing; ResolvedStatus taxonomy where missing/zero tests yield NO/UNKNOWN/F2P_FAILED, never FULL) evaluates resolved=False in EVERY state - I confirmed by simulation that both the base state (0/2 F2P) and the oracle/reference solution (0/340 character-F2P) come out unresolved. The stringified shape is a serialization artifact (swebench's get_dataset 'convert lists to json strings'); the official pipeline feeds real lists to make_test_spec, which is why this mismatch only breaks this task's re-implemented grader. A solution that faithfully follows the instruction - including the shipped reference solution - still fails, which is the defining case of an instruction/verifier mismatch. Secondary observations (not the primary defect): (a) the verifier is not too weak - it fails even the correct fix, the opposite of passing a fabricated answer; (b) the 166 prose-looking PASS_TO_PASS entries are actually matchable because the verbose runner prints docstring first lines verbatim as test lines (verified: 'Staff_member_required decorator works with an argument ... ok'), so with correctly decoded lists the data is internally consistent (base -> unresolved, oracle -> resolved, 335/335 P2P pass); (c) no ANSWER-LEAK to the agent - the oracle patch and hints live only in tests/config.json, which is verifier-side (tests/.dockerignore and the agent image build exclude it); (d) no INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH - the environment runs the full suite in ~16s and provides everything the instructions need.

The shipped environment has no working network: /etc/resolv.conf is 0 bytes (no DNS), outbound TCP to 8.8.8.8:53, 1.1.1.1:443 and 9.9.9.9:53 all time out, no proxy or mirror is configured, the uv cache is empty (28K), and no swebench package/wheels exist anywhere on disk. Running the parser exactly as the verifier does fails with 'Failed to fetch: https://pypi.org/simple/swebench/ ... dns error', exit code 2. Because test.sh uses 'set -uo pipefail', the pipeline 'uv run parser.py | tee' propagates that non-zero code, writes reward 0, and exits non-zero - so even the bundled reference solution is graded FAILED in this environment. The agent cannot resolve this by installing, configuring, or starting any available component: there is no internet to fetch an installer and no local mirror or offline package archive. Earlier verifier stages do work offline (e.g. 'python -m pip install .' succeeds because deps are preinstalled), confirming the hard failure is specifically the PyPI-dependent grading step. Per the rubric this is a dependency/service the verifier references that the environment does not actually provide, making the task unverifiable as written; no other category fits (the test logic itself is a genuine, discriminating check, the instruction and verifier are consistent, nothing is leaked, and the task is non-trivial).

The defect is in the verifier's own grading reference data: tests/config.json stores FAIL_TO_PASS and PASS_TO_PASS as JSON-encoded STRINGS rather than the JSON arrays the SWE-bench format and the swebench 4.0.3 harness expect (e.g. "FAIL_TO_PASS": "[\"testing/test_capture.py::TestFDCapture::test_capfd_sys_stdout_mode\"]"). tests/test.sh builds eval_ref from test_spec.FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS (passed through from this datum by make_test_spec) and only exits 0 (reward 1) when get_resolution_status(report) == FULL; under the swebench grading semantics the reference is iterated as a list of test IDs and any entry that does not match a parsed test result counts as NOT_FOUND (not PASSED). With the double-encoded string values, the grading reference degenerates to the string's individual characters (or raises in a stricter harness), none of which can ever be a passing test result, so the resolution status can never be FULL and the verifier returns reward 0 for ANY patch - including the reference solution that fully satisfies the instructions. Corroborating evidence of the corrupted, machine-scraped reference: once json-decoded, PASS_TO_PASS's first entry is '[100%]', which is not a test ID but a token of pytest verbose output; I reproduced it in the actual verifier log, where leaked lines 'PASSED ... [100%]' (from the inner 'pytest -v' runs printed by test_global_capture_with_live_logging / test_capture_with_live_logging, which appear before the short-test-summary section) yield exactly the key '[100%]' from a token[1] line parse, in exactly the leading position seen in config.json. A correct, instruction-faithful fix therefore still fails the verifier: the verifier checks something (reference entries the instructions never mention and no solution can satisfy) that contradicts the instruction, matching INSTR-VERIFIER-MISMATCH. Other categories were ruled out with evidence: not VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK (the underlying test genuinely fails without the fix and the 107 regression tests are real); not INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH (all referenced paths, the repo at the base commit, the conda env, and uv are present and functional; verifier network needs are covered by allow_internet=true); not INSTR-AMBIGUOUS (the issue unambiguously specifies that mode must not contain 'b'); not TASK-TRIVIAL; not ANSWER-LEAK (the fix is absent from the agent-visible environment: no fix commit in the /testbed git history, the issue text contains only a traceback, and the solution/test files live in the hidden /tests and /solution locations). With the double-encoded string values, the grading reference degenerates to the string's individual characters (or raises in a stricter harness), none of which can ever be a passing test result, so the resolution status can never be FULL and the verifier returns reward 0 for ANY patch - including the reference solution that fully satisfies the instructions. Corroborating evidence of the corrupted, machine-scraped reference: once json-decoded, PASS_TO_PASS's first entry is '[100%]', which is not a test ID but a token of pytest verbose output; I reproduced it in the actual verifier log, where leaked lines 'PASSED ... [100%]' (from the inner 'pytest -v' runs printed by test_global_capture_with_live_logging / test_capture_with_live_logging, which appear before the short-test-summary section) yield exactly the key '[100%]' from a token[1] line parse, in exactly the leading position seen in config.json. A correct, instruction-faithful fix therefore still fails the verifier: the verifier checks something (reference entries the instructions never mention and no solution can satisfy) that contradicts the instruction, matching INSTR-VERIFIER-MISMATCH. Other categories were ruled out with evidence: not VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK (the underlying test genuinely fails without the fix and the 107 regression tests are real); not INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH (all referenced paths, the repo at the base commit, the conda env, and uv are present and functional; verifier network needs are covered by allow_internet=true); not INSTR-AMBIGUOUS (the issue unambiguously specifies that mode must not contain 'b'); not TASK-TRIVIAL; not ANSWER-LEAK (the fix is absent from the agent-visible environment: no fix commit in the /testbed git history, the issue text contains only a traceback, and the solution/test files live in the hidden /tests and /solution locations). Note: the swebench 4.0.3 harness itself could not be executed in this offline review (uv run would need PyPI access), so the exact failure mode (per-character NOT_FOUND report vs. harness error) is inferred; the direct, verifiable defect is the reference data in config.json deviating from the list format the harness it invokes consumes, which makes a faithful solution ungradeable as resolved.

reviews.explanation: This is a well-formed SWE-bench debugging task (pytest-dev/pytest#5262: EncodedFile advertises binary mode 'rb+', breaking libraries that check 'b' in out.mode). I verified end-to-end in the live environment: /testbed is at the exact base commit 58e6a09 with pytest 4.5.1.dev3 installed editable in the 'testbed' conda env; the hidden regression test (applied by the verifier from tests/config.json's test_patch) fails at base exactly as the issue describes (AssertionError: 'b' in 'rb+') and passes with the oracle 4-line fix (a 'mode' property on EncodedFile returning buffer.mode with 'b' stripped). Full-suite runs confirm the FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS contract: at base, 'pytest -rA testing/test_capture.py' gives 1 failed (only the new test) + 107 passed + 7 env-skips + 1 xfail; with the fix, 108 passed, 0 failed. The verifier is strong, not weak: test.sh resets testing/test_capture.py to the base commit and re-applies the official test patch (so test-editing and output fabrication cannot game it), runs the repo's real test suite against the agent's tree, and grades via the official swebench 4.0.3 harness (1 FAIL_TO_PASS + 107 PASS_TO_PASS). Notably, PASS_TO_PASS includes test_typeerror_encodedfile_write, which forces the correct fix class (correct advertised mode while write() still rejects bytes) rather than the wrong one (making write() accept bytes). The '[100%]' entry in PASS_TO_PASS is a known SWE-bench dataset artifact: the log lines that generate it ('PASSED ... [100%]' emitted by inner test runs) appear identically in both base and patched runs (3 occurrences each, verified in both logs), so the harness parser consistently maps it to PASSED, exactly as it did when the dataset was constructed; it does not block resolution. No answer leak: the agent sees only the GitHub issue text (no diff, no fix code, no ground-truth file) and a pristine base repo; the solution patch and test patch live only in the hidden tests/ and solution/ folders. Not ambiguous (the issue precisely defines the required behavior and any implementation achieving it passes), not trivial (requires locating EncodedFile in _pytest/capture.py and understanding that 'mode' is currently delegated to the underlying buffer via __getattr__), and the environment provides everything the instruction and verifier reference (repo, conda env, uv, /logs, network allowed for the parser step), so no environment mismatch.

I verified end-to-end in the task's real environment: /testbed holds the pytest repo at the exact base commit 58e6a09d with an editable install in the conda 'testbed' env (setup.sh pins the commit and the repo's git history stops at the base, so the fix is not recoverable from history - no ANSWER-LEAK; the gold patch exists only in the hidden, separately-run verifier files tests/config.json and solution/solve.sh). The verifier applies a hidden regression test (TestFDCapture::test_capfd_sys_stdout_mode: assert "b" not in sys.stdout.mode under capfd) and grades the full testing/test_capture.py run via the swebench 4.0.3 harness with FAIL_TO_PASS=[that test] and PASS_TO_PASS=107 capture tests. Empirically: without the fix the new test FAILS (sys.stdout.mode is 'rb+' proxied from the underlying buffer via EncodedFile.__getattr__), giving '1 failed, 107 passed' -> verifier fails (not VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK). With the oracle fix (mode property returning self.buffer.mode.replace('b','')) the run gives '108 passed', and every P2P test plus the F2P test is PASSED -> verifier passes; I confirmed test-by-test that exactly the 107 P2P + 1 F2P tests pass. The 7 skipped / 1 xfailed tests (lsof unavailable, python2-only, windows-only) are all absent from PASS_TO_PASS, so environment-specific skips cannot block resolution (not INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH; the pip/uv steps needing PyPI are covered by allow_internet=true, and the config is a standard SWE-bench dataset record whose string-encoded test lists the harness is designed to decode). The instruction (the GitHub issue) explicitly states the required behavior - mode must not advertise 'b' - which is exactly what the regression test checks, and the P2P list is a standard regression guard for the capture module; a faithful fix passes and the verifier first restores testing/test_capture.py from the base commit, so test-file tampering cannot cheat it (not INSTR-VERIFIER-MISMATCH, not INSTR-AMBIGUOUS). reviews.explanation: The instruction (the verbatim GitHub issue in instruction.md) embeds a complete, working solution to the task. Its '#### Fix' section states: 'I propose to use np.sqrt(tk / pk) * np.sqrt(tk / qk) instead, which gives same result and ensuring not bypassing int32', and the issue also names the exact file (sklearn\metrics\cluster\supervised.py), the exact line number (859), and the exact buggy expression 'return tk / np.sqrt(pk * qk) if tk != 0. else 0.' I verified empirically in the actual environment (/testbed at base commit 97523985b39, conda env 'testbed', sklearn 0.20.dev0, numpy 1.19.2): (1) unmodified, the verifier's FAIL_TO_PASS test test_int_overflow_mutual_info_fowlkes_mallows_score fails because fowlkes_mallows_score returns nan with an overflow warning, so the verifier is genuinely tied to the bug; (2) after applying ONLY the one-line replacement prescribed in the instruction (no other changes; in this version contingency_matrix already returns int64, so the issue's fix alone suffices), all 17 tests in sklearn/metrics/cluster/tests/test_supervised.py pass, including the FAIL_TO_PASS test and all 16 PASS_TO_PASS tests, with a mathematically correct FMI value (0.7289959776021899). Thus an agent that merely follows the instruction's recipe can pass the verifier without doing the debugging the task purports to test (diagnosing the integer-overflow root cause and designing a fix); the remaining work is mechanical application of a prescribed line change. Secondary/ruled-out: TASK-TRIVIAL applies secondarily (triviality is caused by the embedded answer); VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK does not apply (the check is behavioral, FAIL_TO_PASS fails pre-fix, and PASS_TO_PASS value/property tests such as test_fowlkes_mallows_score and test_fowlkes_mallows_score_properties would catch a constant-return hack); INSTR-VERIFIER-MISMATCH, INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH, and INSTR-AMBIGUOUS do not apply (environment provides the repo at the exact base commit with a working sklearn install, and the verifier asserts exactly the issue's 'Expected Results' of a finite float instead of nan).

reviews.explanation: The instruction (instruction.md, the GitHub issue text) embeds the complete solution verbatim, so no genuine debugging work is required. The 'Description' section quotes the exact buggy line with file and line number ('sklearn\metrics\cluster\supervised.py:859  return tk / np.sqrt(pk * qk) if tk != 0. else 0.') and the 'Fix' section states the exact replacement ('I propose to use np.sqrt(tk / pk) * np.sqrt(tk / qk) instead'). I verified empirically in the original environment (/testbed at base commit 9752398, sklearn 0.20.dev0, numpy 1.19.2, scipy 1.5.2): (1) at the base commit the FAIL_TO_PASS test fails as expected (RuntimeWarning 'overflow encountered in long_scalars' -> nan -> ValueError in assert_all_finite); (2) applying ONLY the one-line formula change proposed in the issue's Fix section makes the verifier's entire test run pass - all 17 tests in sklearn/metrics/cluster/tests/test_supervised.py, including test_int_overflow_mutual_info_fowlkes_mallows_score (FAIL_TO_PASS) and all 16 PASS_TO_PASS tests; (3) the gold patch's second hunk, .astype(np.int64), is a no-op in this environment because contingency_matrix already returns an int64 matrix (verified c.dtype == int64), and astype applied WITHOUT the formula change still fails the test (pk*qk ~= 1.7e19 overflows even int64) - proving the formula change, i.e. the exact line quoted in the issue, is the entire effective fix. Thus an agent can pass by copying the line proposed in the instructions into the file and line the instructions name, with no exploration or problem-solving. The verifier itself is not weak (real behavioral overflow test plus 16 regression tests) and there is no instruction/environment mismatch; the resulting 'just apply the given one-liner' triviality is a direct consequence of the leak, making ANSWER-LEAK the primary defect.

reviews.explanation: This is a SWE-bench conversion of scikit-learn issue #14983 (repr of RepeatedKFold/RepeatedStratifiedKFold shows a memory address). The environment works and the verifier is strong (it applies the official test patch and requires 2 FAIL_TO_PASS tests plus 105 PASS_TO_PASS tests in sklearn/model_selection/tests/test_split.py via the swebench harness), so it is not VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK, TASK-TRIVIAL, or INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH, and no answer is leaked to the agent (the fix diff appears only in hints_text inside the hidden tests/config.json). The primary defect is a direct contradiction between the instruction's stated expected output and the exact string the verifier asserts: instruction.md's 'Expected Results' block specifies repr(RepeatedKFold()) == 'RepeatedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=10, random_state=None)' (n_splits before n_repeats), but the verifier's FAIL_TO_PASS test asserts the exact string '{}(n_repeats=6, n_splits=2, random_state=None)' (n_repeats before n_splits). I verified this empirically in the real environment (/testbed at base commit 06632c0d, conda 'testbed' env): (1) unpatched, the bug reproduces and the new test fails; (2) a solution faithfully implementing the instruction's literal Expected Results (emitting n_splits, n_repeats, random_state in that order) produces repr(RepeatedKFold()) == 'RepeatedKFold(n_splits=5, n_repeats=10, random_state=None)' exactly as instructed, yet BOTH FAIL_TO_PASS tests fail, so the verifier reports FAILED; (3) only a solution emitting parameters in alphabetical order passes — an ordering requirement that is nowhere stated in the instruction and results solely from the internal behavior of the existing _build_repr helper (line 2148: args = sorted([...]), which sorts 'n_repeats' before 'n_splits'); the reference solution (add __repr__ returning _build_repr(self) plus a cvargs fallback) passes all 107 tests. Thus the verifier asserts a hardcoded value (parameter order) that conflicts with the value the instruction explicitly shows, and a solution that faithfully follows the instruction still fails — the defining condition of INSTR-VERIFIER-MISMATCH. reviews.explanation: The task is a SWE-bench-style debug job (fix Sphinx issue #8459: autodoc_type_aliases ignored when autodoc_typehints='description'). The environment itself is sound and the task genuinely solvable: /testbed is at base commit 68aa4fb with a working conda 'testbed' env (py3.9, tox, pytest, editable Sphinx install) and the required test data (tests/roots/test-ext-autodoc/target/annotations.py with myint). I verified end-to-end: at base the FAIL_TO_PASS test test_autodoc_typehints_description_and_type_aliases fails with exactly the reported bug (renders 'int' instead of 'myint'), and the reference one-line fix (passing type_aliases=app.config.autodoc_type_aliases to inspect.signature in sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py) makes it pass with all 17 PASS_TO_PASS tests green (18 passed). However, the verifier cannot credit even this faithful, correct solution, so it still fails for any agent. Primary defect: tests/test.sh runs 'tox --current-env -epy39 -v -- tests/test_ext_autodoc_configs.py', where the -v flag is consumed by tox, not pytest; pytest actually runs as 'python -X dev -m pytest --durations 25 tests/test_ext_autodoc_configs.py' (confirmed in the recorded log; no addopts in setup.cfg, no PYTEST_ADDOPTS). I ran this exact command with the reference patch applied and inspected the recorded log: pytest printed only dot progress, and the log contains zero occurrences of 'PASSED', 'FAILED', or 'SKIPPED' (only a lowercase '18 passed' summary). The grading step then feeds that log to the swebench 4.0.3 harness (get_logs_eval), which derives per-test statuses from per-test '<test id> PASSED/FAILED/SKIPPED' lines (the swebench harness adds -v/-rA to its own eval commands precisely so these lines exist). With no status lines present, no FAIL_TO_PASS/PASS_TO_PASS test is ever marked passed, 'resolved' stays False, and the verifier writes reward.txt=0 and prints FAILED even with the oracle solution. The verifier thus effectively demands a log format that the instructions never imply and that its own test phase does not produce - a faithful solution still fails, and no agent action can fix this (test.sh is fixed verifier code, hidden from the agent). Secondary defect (INSTR-ENV-MISMATCH): the grading step 'uv run parser.py' must download swebench==4.0.3, datasets==2.16.1 and fastcore<1.11 at verify time, but this environment (the task's original workspace/setup) has no network (DNS resolution of pypi.org/astral.sh fails; 'uv run' aborts after retries) and no copy of those packages or wheels/cache exists anywhere on the filesystem, so the parser cannot even run here; the verifier references a dependency/network service the environment does not provide and which the agent cannot supply. Ruled out: VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK (it does not pass without the fix; it runs the real full sphinx test suite, not shape/keyword checks); INSTR-AMBIGUOUS (the bug to fix is unambiguous); TASK-TRIVIAL (a genuine upstream Sphinx bug requiring real diagnosis); ANSWER-LEAK (workspace is the pre-fix base commit, no solution/test/ground-truth files visible to the agent).

Evidence, all reproduced in the original workspace (/testbed at base commit 68aa4fb, conda 'testbed' env): (1) The hidden test itself is fine and behavioral — with the base code 'test_autodoc_typehints_description_and_type_aliases' fails (rendered param types 'int' instead of 'myint'; 1 failed / 17 passed), and with the reference one-line fix (inspect.signature(obj, type_aliases=app.config.autodoc_type_aliases) in sphinx/ext/autodoc/typehints.py) the whole file passes 18/18, exactly as run by the verifier's own command 'tox --current-env -epy39 -v -- tests/test_ext_autodoc_configs.py'. (2) However, that command invokes pytest as 'python -X dev -m pytest --durations 25 ...' (flags from /testbed/tox.ini; tox's -v is tox's own verbosity), i.e. WITHOUT -rA/-v. I captured the recorded log for the fully-solved (oracle) run: it contains ZERO uppercase per-test result tokens (grep -c for PASSED/FAILED/ERROR/SKIPPED all return 0; the only result info is the lowercase summary line '18 passed, 134 warnings' plus duration lines with no status). The swebench grading used by test.sh (get_logs_eval -> get_eval_tests_report -> get_resolution_status, swebench==4.0.3) determines per-test outcomes by scanning such per-test result lines — which is exactly why official SWE-bench test commands run pytest with -rA. With no 'PASSED tests/...' lines in the success log, the evaluator returns an empty test-status map (found=False), 'resolved' stays False, test.sh prints FAILED and exits 1, and reward.txt gets 0 — even for the reference solution. The failing (unsolved) log, by contrast, does contain a 'FAILED tests/...::test_autodoc_typehints_description_and_type_aliases' line, so the verifier correctly rejects unsolved code but can never accept solved code: the pass criterion implicitly requires the pytest log format to be changed (e.g. adding -rA to the repo's tox.ini), which the instruction (a GitHub bug report) does not imply at all. Secondary (non-effective) issues: the hidden test patch omits the dedicated fixture root 'tests/roots/test-ext-autodoc/autodoc_typehints_description_and_type_aliases/' referenced by srcdir= (it is absent at the base commit and the applied test patch only touches tests/test_ext_autodoc_configs.py); this turns out harmless only because sphinx's app_params fixture falls back to copying the entire 'test-ext-autodoc' testroot, which already contains the required target/annotations.py (myint = int; sum(x: myint, y: myint) -> myint) — verified by the test actually building and discriminating. Not VERIFIER-TOO-WEAK (it does not pass without the fix, and in fact passes for no solution), not an environment gap (repo, env, tox, and grader dependencies are all present and functional), not ambiguous, trivial, or leaked.
